questions.question: Identify the reason for formation of dental plaque.

options.text: When acids stick to the teeth
Masses of bacterial cells together with food particles stick to the teeth
When bacteria acting on sugars produce acids

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Masses of bacterial cells together with food particles stick to the teeth**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Masses of bacterial cells together with food particles stick to the teeth** are the primary reason for the formation of dental plaque.
 
• Dental plaque is a sticky, colorless or pale yellow film that is constantly forming on your teeth.
 
• Plaque is made up of bacteria and food particles. When you consume foods or drinks that contain sugars or starches, the bacteria in plaque produce acids that attack tooth enamel.
 
• If plaque is not removed by regular brushing and flossing, it can harden into tartar (calculus), which can lead to gum disease and cavities.
 
• Maintaining good oral hygiene by brushing twice a day, flossing daily, and visiting the dentist regularly can help prevent the formation of plaque and tartar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saliva** helps to wash away food particles and neutralize acids produced by bacteria in the mouth, which helps to protect against plaque buildup.
 
• **Fluoride**, found in many dental products and drinking water, helps to strengthen tooth enamel and prevent decay.
 
• **Regular dental check-ups** can help identify and treat plaque and tartar buildup before it leads to more serious dental issues.
 
• Some **foods and beverages**, such as sugary snacks and drinks, can contribute to plaque formation and should be consumed in moderation.
 
• Using **antibacterial mouthwash** can also help reduce the number of bacteria in the mouth that contribute to plaque formation.

questions.question: Which of the following books is written by Rabindranath Tagore?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nationalism**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nationalism** is a notable work by Rabindranath Tagore.
 
• Rabindranath Tagore was a prolific writer, poet, and philosopher from India who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.
 
• His works often explore themes of humanism, nationalism, and the intersection of Eastern and Western thought.
 
• Tagore's literature and poetry significantly contributed to the Indian cultural renaissance and inspired many during the Indian independence movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Rabindranath Tagore was born on **7th May 1861** in Calcutta, India.
 
• He is also known for composing the national anthems of India and Bangladesh.
 
• Tagore's literary works include novels, essays, short stories, travelogues, dramas, and thousands of songs.
 
• Some of his other famous works include **Gitanjali**, **Gora**, and **Ghare-Baire**.
 
• In 1915, he was knighted by the British Crown, but he renounced the knighthood in protest of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in 1919.

questions.question: Indian musician, composer and singer Shubha Mudgal was awarded with the ___________ in 2000.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Padma Shri**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Indian musician, composer, and singer **Shubha Mudgal** was awarded the **Padma Shri** in the year 2000.
 
• The **Padma Shri** is the fourth highest civilian award in the Republic of India.
 
• It is awarded to citizens of India in recognition of their distinguished contribution in various spheres of activity including the arts, education, industry, literature, science, sports, medicine, social service, and public affairs.
 
• Shubha Mudgal is renowned for her contributions to Indian classical music, as well as her work in popular music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Padma Awards** are one of the highest civilian honors of India announced annually on the eve of Republic Day.
 
• The awards are given in three categories: **Padma Vibhushan** (for exceptional and distinguished service), **Padma Bhushan** (for distinguished service of a high order), and **Padma Shri** (for distinguished service).
 
• The **Padma Shri** award was instituted in the year 1954.
 
• Shubha Mudgal has also been recognized for her contributions to Indian music with several other accolades and awards throughout her career.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about privatisation is FALSE?

options.text: Improved performance is one of the advantages of privatisation.
There is no possibility of exploitation of monopoly power by private companies after privatisation.
There was an increase in the cases of disinvestment after the economic reforms of 1991 as compared to the pre-1991 period.
Maruti Udyog Limited was a public sector enterprise before the 1991 economic reforms.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**There is no possibility of exploitation of monopoly power by private companies after privatisation.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 2** is false because privatization can lead to the exploitation of monopoly power by private companies, especially in sectors where competition is limited.
 
• **Improved performance** is often cited as an advantage of privatization as private companies may operate more efficiently than public sector enterprises.
 
• There was indeed an **increase in disinvestment** cases after the economic reforms of 1991, aimed at reducing the fiscal burden and improving public sector efficiency.
 
• **Maruti Udyog Limited** was a public sector enterprise before the 1991 economic reforms, after which it saw significant privatization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Privatization involves transferring the ownership of businesses from the public sector (government) to the private sector (businesses or private individuals).
 
• The main objectives of privatization include improving efficiency, reducing government debt, and increasing the competitiveness of businesses.
 
• Economic reforms in 1991 in India included liberalization, privatization, and globalization, collectively known as LPG reforms, which aimed to make the Indian economy more market-oriented and expanding the role of private and foreign investment.
 
• While privatization can lead to better management and more efficient use of resources, it can also result in job losses, reduced public accountability, and potential exploitation in the absence of adequate regulatory frameworks.

questions.question: As of 2022, according to the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas of the Government of India, how many oil refineries are there in India in total?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**23**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas of the Government of India, there are **23 oil refineries** in India as of 2022.
 
• These refineries are a mix of both public sector and private sector enterprises.
 
• The oil refineries are strategically located across different states to cater to the energy needs of the country.
 
• India's oil refining capacity plays a crucial role in ensuring energy security and meeting the domestic demand for petroleum products.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) are some of the major public sector companies operating oil refineries in India.
 
• Reliance Industries Limited and Nayara Energy are key private sector players in the oil refining sector.
 
• India is not only self-sufficient in refining petroleum products but also exports a significant amount of its refined products to various countries.

questions.question: Which of the following physiographic divisions of India has extensive alluvial soil ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The North Indian Plain**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The North Indian Plain** is the physiographic division of India that has extensive alluvial soil.
 
• The alluvial soil in the North Indian Plain is primarily deposited by rivers like the Ganges, Yamuna, and their tributaries.
 
• This soil is highly fertile and suitable for the cultivation of crops such as wheat, rice, sugarcane, and pulses.
 
• The North Indian Plain stretches across several states, including Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and West Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alluvial soil** is formed by the deposition of sediments brought down by rivers.
 
• It is rich in nutrients such as phosphoric acid, potash, and lime, which are essential for plant growth.
 
• The North Indian Plain is also known as the Indo-Gangetic Plain, highlighting its formation through the alluvial deposits of the Indus and Ganges river systems.
 
• Due to its fertility and favorable climate, the North Indian Plain is one of the most densely populated regions in India.

questions.question: What is the shape of the eyeball?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Spherical**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The shape of the eyeball is **spherical**.
 
• This spherical shape allows the eye to have a wide range of motion and helps in the proper focusing of light onto the retina.
 
• The spherical structure is crucial for maintaining the eye's internal pressure and overall health.
 
• Any significant deviation from this shape can lead to vision problems, such as astigmatism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The human eye is approximately 24 millimeters in diameter.
 
• The eye consists of several important parts, including the cornea, lens, retina, and optic nerve, all of which contribute to vision.
 
• Regular eye check-ups are essential for maintaining ocular health and detecting any changes in the shape or condition of the eyeball.
 
• Conditions like myopia (nearsightedness) and hyperopia (farsightedness) are related to the shape of the eyeball.

questions.question: The Swaran Singh committee had formulated ________-point code of fundamental duties.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8-point code of fundamental duties**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Swaran Singh Committee was appointed by the Government of India in 1976 to make recommendations for fundamental duties of citizens.
 
• The committee recommended an **8-point code of fundamental duties** to be included in the Constitution of India.
 
• These duties were intended to serve as a constant reminder to every citizen that while enjoying their rights, they also have a duty to observe certain basic norms of democratic conduct and behavior.
 
• The recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee were incorporated into the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The fundamental duties are enshrined in Part IV-A of the Constitution of India under Article 51A.
 
• Initially, ten fundamental duties were added, but later an eleventh duty was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.
 
• These duties are moral obligations of all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.
 
• Unlike fundamental rights, fundamental duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by the courts for their violation.

questions.question: Prof M Yunus won the Nobel peace prize in which year?

• His work has helped millions of people, especially women, escape poverty by providing small loans without requiring collateral.
 
• The Nobel Committee awarded him the prize for his efforts to create economic and social development from below.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Prof Yunus has received numerous other awards and honors for his contributions to society.
 
• In addition to the Nobel Peace Prize, he has been awarded the **Presidential Medal of Freedom** and the **Congressional Gold Medal** in the United States.

questions.question: The adoption of the industrial policy of 1956 coincided with which Five-Year Plan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2nd Five-Year Plan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The adoption of the industrial policy of 1956 coincided with the **2nd Five-Year Plan** in India.
 
• The 2nd Five-Year Plan focused on the development of the public sector and rapid industrialization.
 
• The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 laid down the framework for the development of industries and aimed at establishing a socialistic pattern of society.
 
• This policy categorized industries into three schedules: those exclusively owned by the state, those progressively state-owned, and those left to private sector development.
 
• It emphasized the role of the public sector in controlling the commanding heights of the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **2nd Five-Year Plan** (1956-1961) was based on the Mahalanobis model, which gave priority to heavy industries and aimed to build a strong industrial base.
 
• The plan aimed at increasing the national income by 25% and the per capita income by 11%.
 
• The industrial policy of 1956 played a crucial role in shaping India's industrial landscape and promoting balanced regional development.
 
• It was during this plan that significant projects like the Bhilai Steel Plant, Durgapur Steel Plant, and Rourkela Steel Plant were established.

questions.question: Which of the following classical dance forms is usually concluded with Tarangam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kuchipudi** is a classical dance form from the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The dance is known for its graceful movements and strong narrative/dramatic character.
 
• **Tarangam** is a distinctive feature of Kuchipudi, typically performed towards the end of the dance recital.
 
• During Tarangam, dancers often balance on the edges of a brass plate while executing intricate footwork.
 
• This performance showcases the dancer's control, skill, and ability to maintain balance while performing complex movements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kuchipudi** has its roots in the ancient Hindu Sanskrit text **Natyashastra**, which is considered the foundation of Indian classical dance forms.
 
• The dance form traditionally narrates stories from Hindu epics and mythology, such as the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
 
• Kuchipudi performances often include both solo and group acts, incorporating expressive gestures, intricate footwork, and rhythmic patterns.
 
• The use of facial expressions and hand gestures (mudras) is essential in conveying the story and emotions in Kuchipudi dance.
 
• Renowned Kuchipudi dancers include **Vempati Chinna Satyam** and **Yamini Krishnamurthy**.

questions.question: For which of the following sources of financial resources may financial intermediation NOT be required?

options.text: Borrowing from All India Development Financial Institutions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Family funds**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Family funds** are financial resources that can be obtained directly from family members without the need for financial intermediation.
 
• In contrast, raising equity via public offering, borrowing from banks, and borrowing from All India Development Financial Institutions typically require the involvement of financial intermediaries.
 
• Financial intermediation involves institutions such as banks, investment funds, and development financial institutions that facilitate the channeling of funds from savers to borrowers.
 
• Using family funds can be advantageous as it may involve lower costs and fewer formalities compared to institutional financing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Financial intermediation** is a process by which financial institutions accept savings from individuals and lend them to others, facilitating the allocation of resources in the economy.
 
• Common financial intermediaries include **banks, credit unions, insurance companies, and investment firms**.
 
• Direct financing, such as using family funds, bypasses these intermediaries and can be a quicker way to secure necessary funds.
 
• However, relying solely on family funds may limit the amount of capital available compared to institutional sources.

questions.question: Generally, Directive Principles are ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**positive directions**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Generally, Directive Principles are **positive directions**.
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines or principles given to the federal institutes governing the state of India, to be kept in consideration while framing laws and policies.
 
• They are enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36–51) of the Constitution of India.
 
• These principles aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They also aim to establish social and economic democracy through a welfare state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Directive Principles are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they cannot be enforced by the courts for their violation.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘All the executive action of the Government of a state shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the Governor’?

• **Article 166(1)** of the Indian Constitution states that all executive actions of the Government of a State shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the Governor.
 
• This provision ensures that the Governor, as the nominal head of the state, is the authority in whose name the executive actions are carried out.
 
• The article is part of Chapter II of the Constitution, which deals with the Executive power of the State.
 
• It establishes a formal procedure for the conduct of government business and maintains the constitutional framework of the state executive.
 
• **Article 166(1) **– States that all executive actions of a State Government shall be expressed in the name of the Governor.
 
• **Article 163(1) **– Specifies that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Chief Minister at the head to aid and advise the Governor in the exercise of his functions, except where the Governor is required to act at his discretion.
 
• **Article 164(1)** – Deals with the appointment of the Chief Minister and other ministers by the Governor and states that the ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the Governor.
 
• **Article 165(1)** – Provides for the appointment of the Advocate-General for the State by the Governor and mentions that he shall hold office during the pleasure of the Governor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **High Courts** play a crucial role in the Indian judiciary system, serving as the intermediate appellate courts between the lower courts and the Supreme Court of India.

questions.question: How much will be 59°F in Celsius?

• The Governor can be reappointed or transferred to another state by the President.
 
• The powers and functions of the Governor are similar to those of the President of India at the state level.
 
• The Governor plays a crucial role in the administration and governance of the state, including giving assent to bills passed by the state legislature, issuing ordinances when the legislature is not in session, and ensuring that the state government adheres to the provisions of the Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following committees recommended the fundamental duties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swaran Singh Committee**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Swaran Singh Committee** was appointed by the government in 1976 to make recommendations regarding the fundamental duties of citizens.
 
• Based on the recommendations of this committee, the **42nd Amendment Act** was enacted in 1976, which introduced the concept of fundamental duties to the Indian Constitution.
 
• These fundamental duties were added as **Part IV-A** of the Constitution, specifically under **Article 51A**.
 
• The fundamental duties are intended to serve as a constant reminder to citizens that while enjoying their rights, they also have responsibilities towards the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of fundamental duties is inspired by the Constitution of the former Soviet Union.
 
• Originally, ten fundamental duties were listed, but an eleventh duty was added by the **86th Amendment Act** in 2002.
 
• The fundamental duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation.
 
• Some of the fundamental duties include respecting the Constitution, the national flag, and the national anthem, cherishing the noble ideals of the freedom struggle, and protecting the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
